passages.note: Senate floor concurrence vote on final passage; Stern is in the Ayes list and the tally is 25-13, so the near-unanimous rule does not apply.
passages.actor_quote: Ayes Allen, Atkins, Beall, Bradford, De León, Delgado, Dodd, Galgiani, Glazer, Hernandez, Hertzberg, Hill, Hueso, Jackson, Lara, Leyva, McGuire, Mitchell, Monning, Pan, Portantino, Skinner, Stern, Wieckowski, Wiener

passages.provision_quote: In order to fulfill unmet long-term resource needs, the commission shall establish a renewables portfolio standard requiring all retail sellers to procure a minimum quantity of electricity products from eligible renewable energy resources as a specified percentage of total kilowatthours sold to their retail end-use customers each compliance period to achieve the targets established under this article.
passages.note: Single-subject renewables bill: the operative sections set binding procurement percentages on dated deadlines, with penalties for noncompliance, and no subsidy, tax-credit or permitting mechanism.

rows.reasoning: Stern voted Aye on final passage (concurrence) of SB 100 (2017-2018), a single-subject renewables bill whose operative text directs that the commission "shall establish a renewables portfolio standard requiring all retail sellers to procure a minimum quantity of electricity products from eligible renewable energy resources" and sets dated targets "44 percent by December 31, 2024, 52 percent by December 31, 2027, and 60 percent by December 31, 2030", enforced by penalties. That is the rung reading "Require a shift to clean energy through mandates and firm deadlines"; the bill carries no subsidy, tax-credit or permitting-reform mechanism, so the funding and permitting rungs are excluded.
